entities.summary: Sasanian art, or Sassanid art, was produced under the Sasanian Empire which ruled from the 3rd to 7th centuries AD, before the Muslim conquest of Persia was completed around 651. In 224 AD, the last Parthian king was defeated by Ardashir I. The resulting Sasanian dynasty would last for four hundred years, ruling modern Iran, Iraq, and much territory to the east and north of modern Iran. At times the Levant, much of Anatolia and parts of Egypt and Arabia were under its control. It began a new era in Iran and Mesopotamia, which in many ways was built on Achaemenid traditions, including the art of the period.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sassanid art played a significant role in shaping the artistic and cultural heritage of Persia and Mesopotamia during the Sasanian Empire's four-century reign. Its influence can be seen in the preservation and transmission of Achaemenid traditions, which had far-reaching consequences for the development of Islamic art and architecture.
